source.stem:
The structures of four organic molecules are shown.

Which molecules are structural isomers of structure 1?

packed_tags.subject: science
packed_tags.topic: What counts as a scientific question or test

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Even careless observations provide dependable evidence for deciding what to investigate next.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Observations count as evidence only when they agree with our existing explanation.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Watching a puri puff in a kitchen cannot start scientific exploration; only laboratory observations can.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: An observation can open a new scientific question only if something visibly changes.

intelligence.enrichment: Scientific investigation is systematic and evolving: careful observations can answer one question while opening new questions and guiding further exploration. Observations produce evidence; evidence supports explanations and can lead to deeper questions. The learner explains that scientific investigation is systematic and evolving, so observations can support explanations and open further questions. Science is finished once the first answer is found, and everyday kitchen observations are not real scientific exploration.
